items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: But like I tell you, man, Buster Bailey, Bushell -- you remember Garvin Bushell? ... MR. GREER: He played all the lead instruments.

ctx.x: And we had to be -- you know, it was necessary. We had to be twice as good as them guys, you know. Now you do--- for recognition. You had to be twice as good. Had to be twice as good singing, twice as good dancing, playing the music. It goes to show you. They say no greater compliment in the world than to be imitated, you know. They're all imitating. All of them want to be soul, soul brothers. That's a big joke. If you ain't got no soul you sure ain't going to be down here with your soul gone, you ain't going to…
But like I tell you, man, Buster Bailey, Bushell -- you remember Garvin Bushell?

items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a historical event involving Sonny Greer, Duke Ellington, and Snowden ('Sonny conspired to get everybody to quit the band... turned the band over to Duke'), but does not claim a personal relationship with Sonny Greer himself.

ctx.x: And Toby Hardwick on saxophone and the Sheet, trumpet. Sonny Greer playing drums. So Clarence and I had this big argument and said we'll break up. Clarence had this in mind anyhow. He saw an opportunity. So, he went to Showden and said, 'I've got a job for you.' In the meantime we'd had the entire Polley circuit booked which is six and a half weeks with the act. Now, when we broke up and Clarence

said, 'Go ahead, I got a group. I can take -- I got a group, I'll take over that (unintelligible).' So I said we'll beat him to it. So I got into New York early Monday morning and I went down to the Palace Theater office and told them that Clarence was bringing in a brand new act. I had the original band, which I did have -- the band went with me. I had the original band and he's bringing a brand new band.
